The '''2024 Copa Libertadores final''' was the final match which decided the winner of the [[2024 Copa Libertadores]]. This was the 65th edition of the [[Copa Libertadores]], the top-tier South American continental club [[Association football|football]] tournament organized by [[CONMEBOL]]. The match was played by Brazilian sides [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]] and [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] on 30 November 2024 at the [[Estadio Monumental (Buenos Aires)|Estadio Monumental]] in [[Buenos Aires]], Argentina.<ref name=Venue>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/la-final-de-la-conmebol-libertadores-2024-se-disputara-en-el-estadio-monumental/ |title=La Final de la CONMEBOL Libertadores 2024 se disputará en el Estadio Monumental |trans-title=The 2024 CONMEBOL Libertadores Final will be played at Estadio Monumental |publisher=CONMEBOL |language=es |date=4 October 2024 |access-date=4 October 2024}}</ref>

Botafogo defeated Atlético Mineiro in the match by a 3–1 score to win their first Copa Libertadores title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/botafogo-conquista-la-gloria-eterna/ |title=¡Botafogo conquista la Gloria Eterna! |trans-title=Botafogo conquer the Eternal Glory! |publisher=CONMEBOL |language=es |date=30 November 2024 |access-date=30 November 2024}}</ref> [[Luiz Henrique (footballer, born 2001)|Luiz Henrique]] was elected MVP of the final and of the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=Melhor da final, Luiz Henrique comemora título: 'Estou vivendo um sonho' |url=https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2024/11/30/melhor-da-final-luiz-henrique-comemora-titulo-estou-vivendo-um-sonho.htm |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=UOL |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=Herói da final e eleito melhor da Libertadores, Luiz Henrique desabafa: 'Tentaram acabar comigo' |url=https://oglobo.globo.com/esportes/futebol/botafogo/noticia/2024/11/30/heroi-da-final-e-eleito-melhor-da-libertadores-luiz-henrique-desabafa-tentaram-acabar-comigo.ghtml |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=O Globo |language=pt-br}}</ref> As winners of the competition, Botafogo qualified for the [[2024 FIFA Intercontinental Cup]], the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]] and earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2024 Copa Sudamericana]] in the [[2025 Recopa Sudamericana]]. They also automatically qualified for the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]] group stage.

== Venue ==
[[File:Estadio mas monumental.jpg|thumb|250x250px|The [[Estadio Monumental (Buenos Aires)|Estadio Monumental]] in [[Buenos Aires]] hosted the final.]]
On 13 February 2024, the [[Argentine Football Association]] announced through its social media accounts that CONMEBOL had selected [[Buenos Aires]] as the host city for the final match of the [[2024 Copa Libertadores]], at a stadium to be confirmed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2024/02/13/oficial-la-final-de-la-copa-libertadores-2024-se-disputara-en-buenos-aires/ |title=Oficial: la final de la Copa Libertadores 2024 se disputará en Buenos Aires |trans-title=Official: the 2024 Copa Libertadores final will be played in Buenos Aires |publisher=[[Infobae]] |language=es |date=13 February 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref> From 26 to 30 May 2024, a delegation from CONMEBOL visited three shortlisted stadiums to host the event: [[Estadio Monumental (Buenos Aires)|Estadio Monumental]] in Buenos Aires, [[Estadio Libertadores de América]] in [[Avellaneda]], and [[Estadio Único Diego Armando Maradona]] in [[La Plata]]. The delegation evaluated technical aspects of the stadiums and visited potential training facilities and accommodation sites for the finalist teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/visita-tecnica-en-buenos-aires-final-conmebol-libertadores/ |title=Visita técnica en Buenos Aires – Final CONMEBOL Libertadores |trans-title=Technical visit in Buenos Aires – CONMEBOL Libertadores Final |publisher=CONMEBOL |language=es |date=30 May 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref>

On 4 October 2024, CONMEBOL confirmed Estadio Monumental as the venue for the final match.<ref name=Venue/> This was the first Copa Libertadores final hosted in Argentina since the finals have been played as single matches, as well as the eighth time that a Copa Libertadores final was played at the stadium.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elgrafico.com.ar/articulo/conmebol-libertadores/82048/cuantas-finales-de-copa-libertadores-se-jugaron-en-el-monumental |title=Cuántas finales de Copa Libertadores se jugaron en el Monumental |trans-title=How many Copa Libertadores finals were played at the Monumental |publisher=[[El Gráfico (Argentina)|El Gráfico]] |language=es |date=4 October 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref>

==Format==
The final was played as a single match at a pre-selected venue, with the higher-seeded team designated as the "home" team for administrative purposes. If scores were level after full time, 30 minutes of extra time would be played. If still tied after extra time, a penalty shoot-out would be used to determine the winner.<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=https://cdn.conmebol.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Manual-de-Clubes-CL-2024-ESP-Digital.pdf|title=Manual de Clubes CONMEBOL Libertadores 2024|publisher=CONMEBOL|access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref>

==Pre-match==

===Opening ceremony===
On the opening ceremony before the kick-off, after a live music and dance performance, [[Djonga]] sang chants of Atlético Mineiro's fans and the club's anthem, and [[Marcelo Adnet]] did the same for Botafogo.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=Abertura da final da Libertadores tem Djonga, Adnet e Djokovic com a taça |url=https://www.band.uol.com.br/esportes/abertura-da-final-da-libertadores-tem-duelo-entre-djonga-e-adnet-e-djokovic-com-a-taca-202411301709 |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=Band |language=pt-BR}}</ref> The trophy of Copa Libertadores was brought to the pitch by Serbian tennis player [[Novak Djokovic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=Djokovic conduz a taça na entrada em campo na final da Libertadores |url=https://ge.globo.com/tenis/noticia/2024/11/30/djokovic-prestigia-a-final-da-libertadores-no-monumental-de-nunez.ghtml |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=ge |language=pt-br}}</ref>

== Match ==
[[Matías Zaracho]] (Atlético Mineiro) and [[Bastos (footballer, born 1991)|Bastos]] (Botafogo) missed the final due to injuries, as well as [[Mateo Ponte]] (Botafogo), who was ruled out due to suspension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=Atlético-MG x Botafogo: onde assistir ao vivo, horário e escalações |url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/libertadores/noticia/2024/11/30/atletico-mg-x-botafogo-onde-assistir-ao-vivo-horario-e-escalacoes.ghtml |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=ge |language=pt-br}}</ref>

=== First half ===
29 seconds into the match, Botafogo midfielder [[Gregore]] hit [[Fausto Vera]] on the head with the sole of his boot during a dispute for the ball in midfield, and received a straight [[Red card (football)|red card]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Atlético-MG 1 x 3 Botafogo {{!}} Taça Conmebol Libertadores: melhores momentos |url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/libertadores/jogo/30-11-2024/atletico-mg-botafogo.ghtml |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=ge |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=Botafogo supera expulsão no início, vence Atlético e conquista Libertadores |url=https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2024/11/30/botafogo-x-atletico-mg-copa-libertadores-da-america-2024.htm |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=UOL |language=pt-br}}</ref> In the following minutes, Botafogo reorganized itself with ten men without its manager [[Artur Jorge (footballer, born 1972)|Artur Jorge]] making any substitutions, and handed the ball over to Atlético Mineiro, who only managed to pose any danger with two shots from afar by [[Hulk (footballer)|Hulk]], defended by [[John (footballer)|John]]. Afterwards, the Rio de Janeiro club loosened up, went on the attack, and in the 35th minute, a play by [[Thiago Almada]] resulted in a shot by [[Marlon Freitas]] that hit [[Junior Alonso]] in the penalty area, and its rebound reached [[Luiz Henrique (footballer, born 2001)|Luiz Henrique]], who finished with force and scored the first goal of the final.<ref name=":0" /> Less than ten minutes later, after a back pass to Atlético goalkeeper [[Everson (footballer, born 1990)|Éverson]], Luiz Henrique pressed, overcame [[Guilherme Arana]]'s marking and protected the ball until he reached the penalty area, when he was fouled by the goalkeeper and suffered a penalty, which was given after the referee's review using [[Video assistant referee|VAR]]. [[Alex Telles]] took a powerful cross shot with his left foot, displacing Éverson and making it 2-0 for Botafogo at the end of the first half.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
[[File:2017 Confederation Cup - CMRCHI - Eduardo Vargas.jpg|thumb|326x326px|[[Eduardo Vargas]] scored for Atlético right after coming in at half-time, but later wasted two clear goal chances.]]

=== Second half ===
Atlético manager [[Gabriel Milito]] made substitutions at half-time and returned to the pitch with [[Bernard (footballer)|Bernard]], [[Mariano (footballer, born 1986)|Mariano]] and [[Eduardo Vargas]], reorganizing his team's offensive structure.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> The changes soon took effect, when two minutes into the second half, a corner kick taken by Hulk found Vargas unmarked, and the Chilean striker headed the ball out of John's reach, scoring for the team from Minas Gerais. After the goal, Atlético insistently pressed Botafogo to seek an equalizer, but with little repertoire or effective alternatives even with an extra player.<ref name=":0" /> In the meanwhile, Artur Jorge reinforced the Rio de Janeiro side's marking with the entries of [[Danilo Barbosa]] and [[Fernando Marçal|Marçal]].<ref name=":1" /> The most dangerous plays of the Minas Gerais club came with Hulk on the right wing, and with Mariano passing to Vargas and [[Alan Kardec]], who wasted chances in front of John. Vargas also missed another opportunity in the 88th minute, when he tried to lob the goalkeeper after a mistake by [[Adryelson]].<ref name=":0" /> In the final minutes, Botafogo sought counterattacks with [[Júnior Santos (footballer, born 1994)|Júnior Santos]] amidst Atlético's pressure, and the strategy paid off when, in the 97th minute, he received a long kick on the right, dribbled past two Atlético players, tried to cross to [[Matheus Martins]] and got the rebound, pushing it into the empty goal and sealing both the victory of the team from Rio de Janeiro and his position as top scorer of the competition, with ten goals.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
